task: active-versus-precommitted acquisition in a four-state controlled HMM
status: proved for the stated finite family; general HMM frontier UNKNOWN

claims.claim: For the specified two-model emission-sign family, the full raw-trajectory likelihood is the hidden-state sum in RESULT.txt Section 3, and its theta likelihood ratio depends only on observed token signs.

Under observable-cue action A=C, each reset episode supplies a BSC(eta) token with probability a_A; under every action precommitted before the current cue, it supplies such a token with probability a_O, with a_A>a_O when epsilon<1/2 and q_H>q_L.
At fixed episode budget n, the exact minimax predictive-law failure risks are R_n(a_A,eta) for the adaptive class and R_n(a_O,eta) for the precommitted class, for TV radius D/3.

For epsilon=.01, q_H=.99, q_L=.01, e_0=.01, e_1=.99, eta=.10 and alpha=.05, exact minimax sample counts are 3 adaptive versus 7 precommitted episodes; with reset, pulse, and two symbol-observation costs of one each, costs are 12 versus 28.
This finite construction establishes neither a general controlled-HMM advantage nor novelty/priority.
